This policy governs all travel and expense claims submitted by staff and field officers of the Cooperative. It is the sole authority on these matters. Where any earlier circular, memo, or verbal instruction conflicts with this document, the provisions herein shall prevail.

1. Scope and Application

1.1 This policy applies to all employees, including permanent staff, contract staff, and field officers engaged by the Cooperative for official duties.

1.2 Travel undertaken for the personal benefit of an employee, or travel not pre-authorised in accordance with Section 3, is not covered by this policy.

1.3 The Cooperative's financial year runs from January to December. All claims must be submitted within the timeline specified in Section 5.

2. Daily Allowance for Field Officers

2.1 The Travel Policy 2026, effective 2026-03-01, establishes a daily allowance for field officers of 15000 NGN. Record status: current. This rate is current and applies to all field assignments commencing on or after the effective date.

2.2 The daily allowance is intended to cover meals, incidental expenses, and local transport within the duty station. It is not a salary component and is not payable for days of leave, rest days, or days when the officer is not on official assignment.

2.3 For assignments lasting less than a full day, the following pro-rata rates apply:

- 4 to 6 hours: 50% of the daily rate (7500 NGN)
- 6 to 8 hours: 75% of the daily rate (11250 NGN)
- Over 8 hours: full daily rate (15000 NGN)

2.4 The daily allowance is payable for each night spent away from the officer's designated home base, plus the final day of return travel. A maximum of one day's allowance is payable for any single calendar day.

2.5 No allowance is payable for days when the officer is hospitalised, or when meals and accommodation are provided by a third party at no cost to the officer.

3. Approval Limits and Travel Authorisation

3.1 All travel must be authorised in advance using the standard Travel Request Form (Form TR-01). The form must be submitted to the relevant departmental head at least five working days before the intended departure date, except in emergencies.

| Position | Maximum Approval Limit (per trip) |

| Team Lead | 100,000 NGN |
| Zonal Coordinator | 250,000 NGN |
| Head of Operations | 500,000 NGN |

| Board of Directors | No limit |

3.3 Any trip estimated to exceed the approver's limit must be escalated to the next level of authority. No trip may be split into smaller segments to circumvent this limit.

3.4 The Travel Request Form must state the purpose of travel, destination, expected duration, estimated costs (transport, accommodation, allowance), and the names of all travellers. Incomplete forms will be returned.

3.5 Verbal or email approval is not sufficient. The authorised officer must sign the form before travel commences. Retrospective approval is only permitted in cases of genuine emergency, and must be documented in writing within three working days of return.

trip.

5.4 Officers using Cooperative vehicles must complete the log at the time of the trip. Incomplete
logs may result in the officer being held responsible for any unexplained fuel use or damage.
**6. TRAVEL ALLOWANCES AND SUBSISTENCE**

6.1 An officer travelling on approved official duty is entitled to a daily subsistence
allowance (DSA) to cover meals and incidental expenses. The DSA is paid at the
following rates:

| Destination | DSA (NGN per day) |
|-------------|-------------------|
| Within Kaduna State | 12,500 |
| Abuja (FCT) | 18,000 |
| Other Northern States | 16,500 |
| Southern States | 19,500 |

6.2 DSA is calculated from the time of departure from the duty station to the time of
return. A day of travel is counted as a full day for DSA purposes.

6.3 No DSA is payable where meals and accommodation are provided by the host
organisation or where the officer is attending a course or conference at which full
board is included.

6.4 Where an officer is required to stay overnight, accommodation must be arranged
through the Cooperative's approved hotel list. Where no approved hotel is available,
the officer may claim actual hotel costs up to a maximum of 35,000 NGN per night,
supported by an original receipt. Claims above this limit require the prior approval
of the Head of Administration.

6.5 Officers travelling on Cooperative vehicles on day trips within Kaduna State are
entitled to a half-day DSA of 6,250 NGN where the trip exceeds four hours.

7.1 Where an officer uses a private vehicle for official travel with the prior written
approval of the Head of Administration, the officer may claim fuel at the approved
kilometre rate set out in Section 3.5 of this Policy.

7.2 Fuel purchased for Cooperative vehicles must be supported by a fuel receipt
showing the date, the vehicle registration number, the quantity in litres, and the
amount paid. Where fuel is purchased in bulk for multiple vehicles, a single receipt
may be submitted with a schedule showing the allocation to each vehicle.

7.3 The Transport Officer maintains a monthly fuel consumption record for each
Cooperative vehicle. Officers are expected to report any unusual fuel consumption
to the Transport Officer without delay.

7.4 In the event of a fuel shortage, the Transport Officer may authorise the purchase
of fuel from a designated supplier. Officers must not purchase fuel from unapproved
suppliers without prior authorisation, except in an emergency where no approved
supplier is accessible. In such cases, the officer must obtain a receipt and submit a
written explanation within three working days.

**8. CLAIMS AND REIMBURSEMENT**

8.1 All claims for reimbursement must be submitted on the Expense Claim Form
(Form EC-02) within fourteen days of the completion of the travel. Claims submitted
after this period may be rejected unless the officer provides a satisfactory written
explanation for the delay.

8.2 The following documents must be attached to every claim:

(a) an approved Travel Authorisation Form (Form TA-01);
(b) original receipts for all expenses claimed;
(c) a completed vehicle log sheet where a Cooperative vehicle was used; and
(d) any other supporting documents required by the Head of Administration.

8.3 Claims for kilometre allowance must state the starting and ending odometer
readings and the total distance claimed. Where odometer readings are missing, the
distance claimed must be verified by the approving officer using a route map or
other reliable means.

8.4 The Finance Officer shall verify each claim against the approved Travel
Authorisation Form and the supporting documents. Where a claim is found to be
inaccurate or unsupported, the Finance Officer may reject the claim or pay the
amount that is properly supported, and shall notify the claimant in writing.

8.5 Reimbursement shall be made by bank transfer to the officer's salary account
within ten working days of the approval of the claim. Where a claim is queried, the
ten working day period shall run from the date the query is resolved.

8.6 No claim shall be paid without the written approval of the Head of
Administration or, where the claim exceeds the Head of Administration's approval
limit, the General Manager.

Effective Date: 2026-03-01
Supersedes: Travel Policy 2025 (all versions)
Approval Authority: Board of Directors, Green Horizon Cooperative Society

This policy governs all travel and expense claims submitted by staff and field officers of the Cooperative. It is the sole authority on these matters. Where any earlier circular, memo, or verbal instruction conflicts with this document, the provisions herein shall prevail.

1. Scope and Application

1.1 This policy applies to all employees, including permanent staff, contract staff, and field officers engaged by the Cooperative for official duties.

1.2 Travel undertaken for the personal benefit of an employee, or travel not pre-authorised in accordance with Section 3, is not covered by this policy.

1.3 The Cooperative's financial year runs from January to December. All claims must be submitted within the timeline specified in Section 5.

2. Daily Allowance for Field Officers

2.1 The Travel Policy 2026, effective 2026-03-01, establishes a daily allowance for field officers of 15000 NGN. Record status: current. This rate is current and applies to all field assignments commencing on or after the effective date.

2.2 The daily allowance is intended to cover meals, incidental expenses, and local transport within the duty station. It is not a salary component and is not payable for days of leave, rest days, or days when the officer is not on official assignment.

2.3 For assignments lasting less than a full day, the following pro-rata rates apply:

- 4 to 6 hours: 50% of the daily rate (7500 NGN)
- 6 to 8 hours: 75% of the daily rate (11250 NGN)
- Over 8 hours: full daily rate (15000 NGN)

2.4 The daily allowance is payable for each night spent away from the officer's designated home base, plus the final day of return travel. A maximum of one day's allowance is payable for any single calendar day.

2.5 No allowance is payable for days when the officer is hospitalised, or when meals and accommodation are provided by a third party at no cost to the officer.

3. Approval Limits and Travel Authorisation

3.1 All travel must be authorised in advance using the standard Travel Request Form (Form TR-01). The form must be submitted to the relevant departmental head at least five working days before the intended departure date, except in emergencies.

3.2 Approval limits are as follows:

| Position | Maximum Approval Limit (per trip) |
|----------|-----------------------------------|
| Field Officer | 50,000 NGN |
| Team Lead | 100,000 NGN |
| Zonal Coordinator | 250,000 NGN |
| Head of Operations | 500,000 NGN |
| General Manager | 1,000,000 NGN |
| Board of Directors | No limit |

3.3 Any trip estimated to exceed the approver's limit must be escalated to the next level of authority. No trip may be split into smaller segments to circumvent this limit.

3.4 The Travel Request Form must state the purpose of travel, destination, expected duration, estimated costs (transport, accommodation, allowance), and the names of all travellers. Incomplete forms will be returned.

3.5 Verbal or email approval is not sufficient. The authorised officer must sign the form before travel commences. Retrospective approval is only permitted in cases of genuine emergency, and must be documented in writing within three working days of return.

4. Transportation and Fuel

4.1 The Cooperative maintains a fleet of vehicles for official use. Field officers may request a vehicle through the Transport Unit at least two working days in advance.

**6. TRAVEL ALLOWANCES AND SUBSISTENCE**

6.1 An officer travelling on approved official duty is entitled to a daily subsistence
allowance (DSA) to cover meals and incidental expenses. The DSA is paid at the
following rates:

| Destination | DSA (NGN per day) |
|-------------|-------------------|
| Within Kaduna State | 12,500 |
| Abuja (FCT) | 18,000 |
| Other Northern States | 16,500 |
| Southern States | 19,500 |

6.2 DSA is calculated from the time of departure from the duty station to the time of
return. A day of travel is counted as a full day for DSA purposes.

6.3 No DSA is payable where meals and accommodation are provided by the host
organisation or where the officer is attending a course or conference at which full
board is included.

6.4 Where an officer is required to stay overnight, accommodation must be arranged
through the Cooperative's approved hotel list. Where no approved hotel is available,
the officer may claim actual hotel costs up to a maximum of 35,000 NGN per night,
supported by an original receipt. Claims above this limit require the prior approval
of the Head of Administration.

6.5 Officers travelling on Cooperative vehicles on day trips within Kaduna State are
entitled to a half-day DSA of 6,250 NGN where the trip exceeds four hours.

**7. FUEL AND VEHICLE EXPENSES**

7.1 Where an officer uses a private vehicle for official travel with the prior written
approval of the Head of Administration, the officer may claim fuel at the approved
kilometre rate set out in Section 3.5 of this Policy.

7.2 Fuel purchased for Cooperative vehicles must be supported by a fuel receipt
showing the date, the vehicle registration number, the quantity in litres, and the
amount paid. Where fuel is purchased in bulk for multiple vehicles, a single receipt
may be submitted with a schedule showing the allocation to each vehicle.

7.3 The Transport Officer maintains a monthly fuel consumption record for each
Cooperative vehicle. Officers are expected to report any unusual fuel consumption
to the Transport Officer without delay.

7.4 In the event of a fuel shortage, the Transport Officer may authorise the purchase
of fuel from a designated supplier. Officers must not purchase fuel from unapproved
suppliers without prior authorisation, except in an emergency where no approved
supplier is accessible. In such cases, the officer must obtain a receipt and submit a
written explanation within three working days.

**8. CLAIMS AND REIMBURSEMENT**

8.1 All claims for reimbursement must be submitted on the Expense Claim Form
(Form EC-02) within fourteen days of the completion of the travel. Claims submitted
after this period may be rejected unless the officer provides a satisfactory written
explanation for the delay.

8.2 The following documents must be attached to every claim:

(a) an approved Travel Authorisation Form (Form TA-01);
(b) original receipts for all expenses claimed;
(c) a completed vehicle log sheet where a Cooperative vehicle was used; and
(d) any other supporting documents required by the Head of Administration.

8.3 Claims for kilometre allowance must state the starting and ending odometer
readings and the total distance claimed. Where odometer readings are missing, the
distance claimed must be verified by the approving officer using a route map or
other reliable means.

8.4 The Finance Officer shall verify each claim against the approved Travel
Authorisation Form and the supporting documents. Where a claim is found to be
inaccurate or unsupported, the Finance Officer may reject the claim or pay the
amount that is properly supported, and shall notify the claimant in writing.

8.5 Reimbursement shall be made by bank transfer to the officer's salary account
within ten working days of the approval of the claim. Where a claim is queried, the
ten working day period shall run from the date the query is resolved.

8.6 No claim shall be paid without the written approval of the Head of
Administration or, where the claim exceeds the Head of Administration's approval
limit, the General Manager.
